commit.message:
feat(print): poster printing that tiles large pages over smaller sheets (#597)

Add "Poster (tiles)" to the Type list of "Page Placement and Scaling" in the
print dialog. It replaces the scaling choice and pages per sheet, and shows
its own settings: tile scale (100 % keeps the true drawing scale), overlap
in mm, cut marks, labels (file name, page number, tile row,column) and
"tile only large pages".

The geometry lives in a new pure module, js/pdf/print-poster.js, used by
both the preview and the print PDF so they cannot drift:
- grid per page along each axis with overlap, centred over the page;
- the tile window is the printer's printable area, inset by a 7 mm band
  for cut marks and labels when either is on;
- sheet orientation: the fixed one, or with auto rotate the one that
  needs the fewest sheets (ties follow the page);
- cut lines on the page edges and in the middle of each overlap, drawn as
  ticks in the band outside the window; labels in the bottom band, in the
  app language when the standard PDF font can set it, otherwise English;
- pages that fit the paper at tile scale are printed normally (centred,
  shrunk to the printable area if needed, quarter turn on a fixed sheet).

The print job builds the usual print PDF with every page at its own size
(raster and vector paths unchanged) and maakPoster lays the tiles on the
sheets: the page as a form XObject clipped to the tile window. Poster
sheets always go to the printer 1:1. Unknown paper falls back to A4. The
MCP print commands ignore a remembered poster choice and fall back to fit.

Settings are remembered with the other print settings. New strings in all
40 locales. Unit tests cover grid counts for A1/A0 on A4/A3 at several
scales, overlap, printable margins, orientation, tile-only-large, cut mark
and label positions, and a pdf-lib test that checks every tile of the
real print PDF lands where the preview shows it.
Merge branch 'r429/597-poster' into integratie/release-2026.42.9

fix(android): grant the plugin permissions to the main window (#596)

The mobile capability had no "windows" entry, so it applied to no window
at all. On Android every plugin call was refused with "not allowed by
ACL": listening for events (so "open with" while the app runs never
arrived), the locale, the app version, the file dialog and reading the
picked or handed-over file.

Bind the capability to the main window and grant the same permissions as
on the desktop where they make sense on a phone (window title and theme,
store). Reading content:// URIs needs no extra fs scope: the fs plugin
opens them through the ContentResolver.

fix(android): keep preferences and session in the app data directory (#596)

On Android dirs::data_local_dir() points below the read-only root, so
saving preferences and the session failed with "Read-only file system
(os error 30)" and every start was a first start.

At startup on mobile the app's local data directory from the Tauri path
resolver becomes the base for preferences, session and catalogs. The
desktop keeps the OS data directory; OPDS_DATA_DIR still wins everywhere.
The choice is a pure function with unit tests.

fix(android): run PDF.js on older WebViews and drop inline scripts (#596)

Android updates the system WebView separately; an Android 12 device can
still run Chromium 91. PDF.js 6 (also its legacy build) calls APIs that
version lacks without a fallback: Promise.withResolvers threw
"undefined is not a function" in the load task (empty page),
ArrayBuffer.transferToFixedLength made every page with text produce an
empty operator list (white page), and for-await over a ReadableStream
broke the text layer. The worker file also contains a class static
block, which Chromium 91 cannot parse.

- js/core/oude-webview.js fills in only what is missing (also a no-op on
  current WebViews) and is imported before the rest of the app.
- The build lowers the PDF.js worker for Chromium 91 and puts the same
  polyfills in front of it (scripts/oude-webview.mjs).
- The Android WebView adds hashes of its own init scripts to the CSP,
  which disables 'unsafe-inline' and blocked the app's inline theme and
  startup diagnostics script. That script now loads from opds-vooraf.js.

ci(android): sign with a fixed key and keep the app clear of the system bars (#596)

Signing: every release generated a new keystore, so an APK could never
be installed over the previous one ("App not installed",
INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE). The release now signs with the key
in the ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 / ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD /
ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS / ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD secrets, passes the passwords
through the environment, removes the keystore afterwards and prints the
certificate fingerprint. Without the secrets it still builds an APK with
a one-off key and raises a warning.

System bars: the activity runs edge-to-edge (enforced from targetSdk 35)
and the WebView reported no safe-area insets, so the bottom toolbar sat
under the navigation bar (zoom-in pressed Home) and on Android 15 the
top bar under the status bar. src-tauri/android/MainActivity.kt pads the
content view by the system bar, display cutout and keyboard insets. It
also exposes window.OpdsAndroid.displayName(uri) for the display name of
a content:// URI.

gen/android is generated by `tauri android init` and now ignored;
scripts/android-project.mjs copies the activity into it, in the release
workflow right after init.

fix(mobile): open picked files at once, with real names and load errors (#596)

- Returning from the system file picker, the plugin's answer only
  reached the page with the next IPC message: picking a file did nothing
  until the user tapped something else. When the app becomes visible
  again it now sends a small IPC message for a few seconds
  (js/mobile/ipc-wekker.js).
- A document opened from another app or the picker was titled after the
  opaque id of its content:// URI ("19", "msf%3A19"). Tabs, title bar
  and window title now use the display name from Android and otherwise a
  readable name from the URI ("Document.pdf" for a bare id).
- "Failed to load PDF:" showed no reason, because Tauri errors are plain
  strings, not Error objects; the message now shows the string.
- The mobile view has no thumbnail panel, yet all pages were rendered as
  thumbnails on the main thread (tens of seconds of jank on a heavy
  file). Mobile skips them.

feat: view U3D 3D PDFs on the page, with markup pages

i18n(compare): translate split line mode labels in all locales (#603)

Replace the English placeholders for compare.split and compare.splitDesc
with real translations in the 38 remaining ribbon.json locales.

fix(ui): use one central system UI font across the interface (#600)

Only the ribbon and menus followed the operating system font: they are
buttons, which browsers render in the system font, while body text used
a hard-coded 'Segoe UI', Tahoma, Geneva, Verdana stack that falls back to
an unrelated font on Linux and macOS.

- base.css defines --ui-font (system-ui first, then -apple-system,
  Segoe UI, Noto Sans, Ubuntu, Cantarell, Helvetica Neue, Arial,
  sans-serif) and --ui-font-mono on :root; body uses --ui-font and
  button/input/select/textarea/optgroup inherit the family.
- fonts.css no longer sets font-family per language (it was overridden by
  body anyway); script languages now only extend --ui-font with
  script-specific fallbacks after system-ui, via :root:lang().
- Component stylesheets (find bar, mini log, assistant header, sticky
  note popup, shortcut keys, form validation dialog, print preview nav)
  and inline styles (keystroke overlay, parametric symbol picker) use
  var(--ui-font); code, hex values and tokens use var(--ui-font-mono).
- PDF content keeps its own fonts: form fields on the page, the text
  annotation input, canvas text, the B/I/U glyph buttons and the ribbon
  text-style "T" preview.
- Add js/ui/ui-lettertype.test.mjs, a guard that fails when a UI
  stylesheet or component inline style hard-codes a font family instead
  of the variables, with a documented allowlist.
Merge branch 'r4210/600' into integratie/release-2026.42.10

feat(properties): show and choose the unit for image width/height (#598)

Image Width and Height in the properties panel now show their unit and
let the user pick mm, cm, in or pt. The model stays in page points; the
unit is display only, so switching it never changes the size or position
of an image and adds no undo step.

- New pure module annotations/papiermaat-eenheid.js: conversion, per-unit
  display precision (at least three significant digits so tiny sizes never
  show as 0), parsing of typed values (dot or comma, intermediate states
  "", "0", "0." return null) and the aspect-lock math for images.
- The typed value is read in the selected unit; with aspect ratio locked
  the partner dimension follows the original ratio in every unit. The
  store keeps the sizes in points instead of the typed text.
- The input is only rewritten while the user is not typing in it, so
  "3.250" or "0." are not reformatted mid-entry.
- New preference paperSizeUnit (default pt), settable from the unit list
  in the panel and from Preferences > Annotations > General; it persists
  across selections and restarts.
- The same unit applies to the scale bar's Bar Height (also a paper
  size, now kept with decimals, minimum 4 pt). Line widths, font sizes
  and arrow head sizes stay in pt by typographic convention.
- New strings in all 40 locales.
- Tests: papiermaat-eenheid.test.mjs (pure module) and
  papier-eenheid-paneel.test.mjs (real properties store under node).

fix(compare): align split line old page with change detection (#603)

- Extract pure helpers (mode normalisation, single-pane check, split
  fraction, old page transform, screen-size px) into split-line.js and
  cover them with unit tests.
- Rotate the OLD page about the NEW page centre with transform-origin 0 0,
  exactly like the change detection, so alignment also matches when the
  two pages differ in size.
- Give the OLD clip strip a white background so an aligned (dx/dy/rot)
  old page never lets the NEW page show through left of the line.
- Clean up the drag listeners on pointercancel as well.
- Normalise unknown compare modes to overlay in startCompare and in the
  toolbar mode switch.

perf(compare): run change detection in a module web worker (#465)

detectChanges() ran a full-page union-find on the main thread and froze
the window on large sheets. It now runs unchanged in a module Web Worker
(change-detect.worker.js), built by Vite via new Worker(new URL(...)).

- change-detect-protocol.js: pure message protocol plus a latest-wins
  client. Request ids come from the existing detection sequence; a request
  overtaken before it reaches the worker is never sent, a late reply is
  reported as stale and only cached, never shown.
- The freshly aligned old buffer is transferred; the cached new raster is
  copied so the raster cache stays intact.
- Without Worker support, or when the worker fails to load or post, the
  client falls back to the same function synchronously and the attempt is
  retried once.
- Detection is skipped when the pair was superseded during rasterisation.

Tests cover the protocol, stale handling, the fallback and result equality
between the direct call and a real worker thread.

fix(render): make Thin Lines thin the page's vector strokes (#595)

The Thin Lines toggle only reached the annotation overlay. The page itself
is rendered in Rust (PDFium workers, the in-process fallback and the tile
scene) and none of those render paths knew about the preference, so vector
strokes kept their full width whether the toggle was on or off, also after
reopening the file.

- PDFium has no thin-line render flag: set the stroke width of every path
  object (form XObjects included) to 0, the hairline width of the PDF
  specification, on the parsed page before rendering. Shared by the worker
  and the in-process renderer (pdfium-worker/src/thin_lines.rs). Workers
  that keep a heavy page open remember the original widths and restore
  them when Thin Lines is switched off.
- render_pdf_page, render_pdf_page_region and render_tile_scene_region take
  a thinLines argument; the worker protocol carries thin_lines (absent =
  off). The tile scene strokes 1 device pixel wide in this mode.
- Every bitmap cache keys on the line mode: the Rust pixmap cache, the page
  bitmap cache, the tile cache and the continuous-view bitmap cache. A
  render keeps the mode it started with, so a result that lands after a
  toggle is filed under its own mode and switching back is a cache hit.
- Ribbon button, the 'tl' command, Ctrl+5 and the preferences dialog go
  through one toggle that saves the preference and re-renders the single
  page view (bitmap + tile) or the visible continuous pages in place.
- The vector replay path strokes one-device-pixel hairlines as well.

fix(3d): harden the U3D decoder against damaged files (#599)

The model stream comes from the PDF and is untrusted. The decoder could
allocate gigabytes or loop for minutes on a few hostile bytes (a face
count of four billion, a node with four billion parents, faces whose
indices cost no bits), and an impossible arithmetic-coder state could
spin the renormalisation loop forever.

- every count is checked against the bits left in its block before
  anything is allocated; reading past a block's end throws
- the arithmetic decoder rejects out-of-range targets and empty intervals
- position indices are checked against the position count
- at most 16 million triangles per file
- a failing block is skipped (scene.skipped) instead of failing the file;
  a mesh that breaks off keeps the faces read in full
- the dynamic context uses a Fenwick tree, so escapes to many distinct
  values stay O(log n) per symbol
- non-finite positions and colours are replaced

Tests write U3D files with an independent writer (block layout, bit
order, static and dynamic arithmetic contexts) and fuzz the reader with
every truncation, random bit flips and random data.

fix(3d): shared meshes, view cameras, markup page boxes and viewer cleanup (#599)

Decoding and drawing:
- a mesh used by several model nodes failed the whole file: the worker
  listed its buffer twice in the transfer list (DataCloneError). Draw
  data now has one geometry per mesh resource, shared by its nodes, and
  a node with several parents is drawn under each (u3d-scene.js)
- faces are ordered by shading group with a counting sort instead of an
  array sort with a comparator
- a plain FlateDecode model stream is inflated in the worker (capped at
  512 MB), not on the main thread
- group parent chains that loop hang off the root
- decoded models are kept for the two most recent 3D pages, so returning
  from a markup page does not decode again; entries of closed documents
  are dropped

Views:
- orthographic views (/P /Subtype /O) use an orthographic camera
- /FOV is converted from its /PS binding (width by default) to the
  vertical field of view
- /3DV and /DV accept an index, /F, /L, /D, an internal name or a view
  dictionary
- the /OPS_3DSnapshot record is checked field by field when read

Markup pages (moved to three-d/snapshot-page.js):
- the page keeps the source page's MediaBox, CropBox and /Rotate, so the
  picture lands on the 3D area also for sheets with offset boxes
- a missing /Rect no longer fails; the page insert is undoable with its
  page mapping
- the page record survives saving and a later save with markups (tested
  against the saver's pattern)

Viewer:
- the expanded view closes when the tab or page changes, so it no longer
  keeps another document's model alive
- right-drag pan no longer opens the page context menu or switches the
  annotation tool; pointer and wheel events stay inside the 3D area
- decode errors and partly read models show a translated message
- Windows-style toolbar: square corners, default cursor
- a document's page operations only rescan for 3D content when the
  document had 3D content

perf(3d): load the 3D viewer only for documents with 3D content (#599)

The viewer component was imported by App.jsx and grew the main chunk by
19 kB. A small shell (ThreeDLazy.jsx) now loads ThreeDView.jsx, and with
it three.js (688 kB) and the orbit controls, only once the active
document has a 3D annotation or a 3D markup page; for other PDFs only
the 4 kB scanner chunk loads. The shell also drops decoded models of
closed documents.

three is pinned to exactly 0.170.0. App.jsx no longer carries the stray
carriage returns of the earlier change.

fix(i18n): translate the 3D view strings into all locales (#599)

The 3D view strings were English in 38 locales. All 40 locales now have
real translations of the 28 keys, including the three new messages for
models that cannot be read, partly read models and a viewer that cannot
start.

feat(assistant): follow the app language in the assistant (#452)

- Move every user-visible assistant text (greeting, header, provider
  status, API key button and placeholder, thinking indicator, input
  placeholder, send button, error messages) into common.assistant in
  all 40 locales.
- Skills are data now: id, icon, needsInput and an English instruction
  for the model. Chip label, tooltip and the text shown in the chat or
  input box come from common.assistant.skills.<id> per language.
- A chip shows the localized text but sends the fixed English
  instruction to the model; for skills that need input the localized
  prefix is swapped for the instruction on send.
- The system prompt is built per request with buildSystemPrompt(): it
  names the app language (English name, native name and code) and tells
  the model to answer in it, so a language change applies to the next
  question. The base skill instructions are English; the relay and API
  key handling are unchanged.
- Add assistant-i18n.test.mjs: keys in all locales, real translations,
  every skill has label/hint/prompt, no hard-coded Dutch in the panel or
  skill file, and the prompt carries the language.

feat(print): booklet printing in saddle-stitch order (#381)

Add "Booklet" to the pages-per-sheet choice of the print dialog. The
pages are arranged for a folded, stapled booklet: two per side of a

  (same rules for the preview and the printed PDF)

- PrintDialog.jsx: booklet option, preview per sheet side with a note

  exclusive with poster and more than one page per sheet

feat(organize): split document by pages, bookmarks or file size (#381)

New "Split Document" button in the Organize ribbon tab with a
Windows-style, movable modal dialog:

- split every N pages, by top-level bookmarks (the bookmark titles
  become the file names) or by a maximum file size in MB (measured on
  the real output, so shared fonts and images count once)
- output folder and a file name pattern with {name}, {n}, {bookmark},
  {start} and {end}; names are sanitized for Windows/macOS/Linux and
  made unique; existing files are only replaced after confirmation and
  files open in the app are never overwritten
- parts are copied with pdf-lib like extractPages and keep their
  annotations, the in-app page rotation, page labels and the bookmarks
  that fall inside the part; links and /P references are re-pointed to
  the part (or dropped) so no pages from other parts are dragged along

Pure logic in splits-logica.js, the pdf-lib part in splits-document.js,
both with unit tests; strings in all 40 locales.

feat(annotations): text model and correction rules for the proofreading mode (#508)

A text model is built from the pdf.js text items of a page: lines in
reading order with every character on its baseline in page space, also
on rotated pages and for rotated text. On top of it:
- cursor movement (characters, lines with a kept column, words,
  line and page start/end), ranges, rectangles per line and hit testing;
- an insert at the cursor (caret), a replace over a selection (caret
  parent plus a linked strike-through child) and a delete as a
  strike-through whose struck text goes into markedText only;
- Delete/Backspace extending the last strike-through, by character or
  by word, over line breaks;
- the Tab order of corrections, the Esc levels and the key map.

Every correction is one undo step. A strike-through that grows with
repeated presses updates its own add step (amendLastAdd), unless the
document was saved after it; then the growth is a modify step.

A save round trip with the real saver and loader converter checks the
kinds, colours, rectangles and directions, the absence of duplicates,
/OPS_MarkedText and /Contents without struck text, and an untouched
page content stream.

feat(annotations): keyboard-driven proofreading mode (#508)

F2, or the Proofreading button on the Annotation tab, switches the
mode on and off. A text cursor moves over the text of the page: arrow
keys, Home/End, Ctrl+arrow by word, Ctrl+Home/End, Page Up/Down to the
previous or next page with text, Shift to select; a click places the
cursor, a drag or double click selects.

- Typing opens an inline input: at the cursor it becomes an insert
  (blue caret), over a selection a replace (purple caret and strike).
  Enter commits, Tab commits and goes on to the next correction.
- Delete/Backspace strike through at once (red); pressing again extends
  the strike, Ctrl strikes by word.
- Tab and Shift+Tab go to the next and previous correction and select it
  as the comments panel does.
- Esc steps back one level: close the input, clear the selection, leave.

While the mode is on its keys are caught first, so no tool shortcut
fires; Ctrl and Alt shortcuts such as undo and save still work. The
cursor and selection are drawn on every page in single page and
continuous view. The inline input follows the Windows style. New
strings are translated in all locales.

commit.message: feat(pdf): preserve Office exports, save targets, and measurement scales
docs: add the English promo kit
feat(print-queue): pure model for job names, paper size and list selection

chore(deps): update PDF.js to 6.4.299

Takes the dependency part of the PR's release commit: pdfjs-dist
6.3.289 -> 6.4.299 with the matching lockfile (including the optional
@napi-rs/canvas 1.0.9 -> 1.0.11), and the PDF.js line in the
technology table. The app version stays at 2026.42.10.

feat(print-queue): recover the printed document name and translate the printer window in all languages

The Windows PDF driver behind the virtual printer writes the print job's
document name to /Info /Title; virtual_printer_jobs now returns it.
Replaces the printQueue strings of the unused in-app queue dialog, which is
removed together with its styles.

fix(pdf): write dimension measure formats per the PDF spec

The rectilinear measure dictionary of a dimension line reused the /X
number format for /D. In /D the conversion factor applies to the /X
units, so other readers multiplied the scale twice, and /D held the
number of decimals where the specification (and the app's own loader)
expects the precision denominator: a line with two decimals reopened
with none.

/X now carries the scale, /D and /A a factor of 1 with 10^decimals as
denominator. A scale taken from the page, a scale region or the
document is still written for other readers, but marked with
OPS_ScaleInherited; the loader then leaves the line without a scale of
its own, so it keeps following the page scale after reopening instead
of freezing it.

The dimension-measure tests are added to the unit test list (they did
not run) and now cover the round trip through the loader.

feat(print-queue): redesign the printer window and the virtual printer tab

Printer window: toolbar with the main actions, a job list with larger
thumbnails, page count, paper size of page 1, file size and time, a page
by page preview of the focused job, a status bar with progress and
results, a confirmation before delete, Explorer-style selection and
keyboard (Enter, Del, Ctrl+A, arrows, Alt+Up/Down), and an empty state
that explains how to print to the printer and links to its settings.
Opening jobs in Studio no longer removes them from the list.

Preferences tab: printer state with an icon and explanation, a short
how-it-works list, and a button that opens the printer window.

A guard test keeps user-visible text out of both components.

test(pdf): run the PDF.js legacy build without the APIs Chromium 91 lacks

A child process removes every API the Android 12 WebView (Chromium 91)
does not have, installs only the app's polyfills and then opens, reads
and renders a real PDF with the legacy build: text content, operator
list and, when @napi-rs/canvas is present, a page render with ink.
Without the polyfills the same run fails, so the check measures
something. PDF.js 6.4.299 passes; core-js inside the legacy build
covers Set methods, iterator helpers, Uint8Array base64/hex,
Promise.try, Math.sumPrecise, getOrInsertComputed and URL.parse, and
PDF.js itself adds Response/Blob.prototype.bytes.

fix(print): honour repeated pages and the chosen orientation in the print preview (#606)

- Custom page ranges are now read as typed for printing: order and repeats
  are kept ("1,1,1" prints page 1 three times, "3,1,2" keeps that order,
  "5-3" runs backwards). The range was parsed as a sorted set, so both the
  preview and the print job (dialog and MCP print command) silently dropped
  repeated pages. Exporting and deleting keep the set semantics.
- With a fixed number of pages per sheet, an orientation confirmed in Page
  Setup now decides the sheet orientation, also with auto-rotate on. Before,
  auto-rotate turned the n-up sheet into "best fit", so the preview and the
  print stayed landscape after choosing portrait. Without a confirmed choice
  the best-fit sheet is still used; the "auto-rotate overrides" note no
  longer shows for n-up because nothing is overridden there.
- Fixed n-up grids (2, 6, ...) may turn a quarter with the sheet when the
  pages come out larger (6 per portrait sheet = 2 x 3); custom grids stay as
  typed. Preview and print use the same rule.

feat(print): flyer printing, booklet signatures and a page order indicator (#607)

- Pages per sheet gets "Flyer (copies per sheet)": every page fills its own
  sheet with 2, 4, 6, 8, 9 or 16 copies, ready to cut, with optional cut
  marks in the sheet margin on the extension of every page edge. It uses
  the same sheet, grid and cell rules as pages per sheet, so the preview
  and the print match; each page is rendered once and repeated on the sheet.
- Booklets can be printed in signatures: "Sheets per signature" (all, or
  1-16 sheets) splits a thick book into stacked saddle-stitched signatures;
  only the last signature is padded with blank pages. The preview note shows
  which signature a sheet belongs to.
- The pages-per-sheet preview shows the page number in every cell and arrows
  along the chosen page order, and a small path icon sits next to the page
  order choice. Both exist only in the dialog, never in the printed output.
- New strings are translated in all 40 locales; the new choices are kept
  with the other print settings.

fix(tabs): tear a tab off into a second app instance without the OS drag loop

Dragging a tab out of the tab bar ran a native OS file drag (DoDragDrop on
the main thread) for every tear-off. On Windows that loop reports "Dropped"
even when the window under the cursor accepts nothing, and "Cancel" (not
"Cancelled") for Escape, so a tab dropped outside the app was closed without
opening anywhere else; the "drop on empty space opens a new window" branch
could never run. The same modal loop is what froze or hard-aborted the whole
app before (#335).

Tearing off is now an ordinary in-WebView drag: released beyond the tab bar
threshold, the tab is closed here (asking to save a modified document first)
and opened in a second app instance started with --new-instance. The OS drag
is only started while the cursor is over another instance of the same app,
to move the tab there; afterwards the window under the cursor decides
between closing, keeping and tearing off.

A second instance skips the single-instance plugin through the explicit
--new-instance flag and leaves the session file, the AI link, the print
queue watcher, the PrtScn hotkey and the default-app check to the primary
instance, so it no longer overwrites the primary instance's session.

feat(thumbnails): add a File Explorer thumbnail handler for PDFs (#605)

New workspace crate open-pdf-thumbnails: an in-process COM server
(IInitializeWithStream + IThumbnailProvider) that renders page 1 with the
bundled pdfium.dll, loaded by full path from the DLL's own folder.

- reads only the IStream it is given; PDFium pulls blocks on demand, so

- size follows the displayed page (after /Rotate), longest side = cx,

- password-protected, empty, broken or non-PDF files return an error so

  handler is only replaced on request and restored exactly afterwards

build(windows): bundle, sign and clean up the thumbnail handler (#605)

- release.yml builds it in both Windows jobs, signs it with the other

- installer: a DLL still loaded by the thumbnail surrogate is renamed
  aside instead of failing the update; uninstall turns the thumbnails off
  for the current user when they point at this install folder (64-bit
  registry view), restoring a replaced handler; updates keep the setting

feat(preferences): show PDF thumbnails in File Explorer as an option (#605)

Preferences > File Association gets a Windows-only checkbox "Show PDF
thumbnails in File Explorer". It reads the real registry state and applies
the change at once (per user, no admin, default PDF app unchanged), then
notifies the shell.

When another program already provides PDF thumbnails, the app asks before
replacing them; turning the option off restores them. A handler of another
default PDF app takes precedence in Windows and is only reported.

New commands explorer_thumbnails_status and explorer_thumbnails_set, texts
in all 40 languages, and unit tests for the wiring and translations.

commit.message:
fix(callout): draw, apply and save start/end line endings (#612)

A callout drew one fixed head at the tip from a field nothing ever
wrote (arrowStyle, so always a closed head of 7), never drew a start
head, and its saved appearance always held an open head of 8. The
Format ribbon Start/End dropdowns only wrote to arrows, the format
store only read arrows, and the Properties panel hid Line Endings for
callouts. The file always got /LE /OpenArrow.

- callout-koppen.js: one pure geometry helper for the leader heads
  (End at the tip, Start where the leader leaves the note box, angles
  for straight and curved leaders, a knee on an end point, stroke
  shortened into filled heads). The screen and the saved appearance
  both use it, at headSize (default 7, as before).
- lijnkoppen.js: lintZetLijnkoppen() for arrow, splineArrow and
  callout (a plain line draws no heads, measurements have their own),
  koppenVan() for the per-type defaults, and the callout file mapping.
  For a FreeText /LE is a single name for the tip (ISO 32000-1, table
  174); both heads also go into /OPS_LineHeads and the size into
  /OPS_HeadSize. Reading accepts /LE as a name or an array; a callout
  saved by the app before this change (/OPS_Rotation, no
  /OPS_LineHeads) keeps the closed head it showed on screen.
- Ribbon, format store and Properties panel use the predicate and show
  the drawn defaults (also the real arrow head size 8 instead of 12).
- /Rect grows with the head size so large heads are not clipped.

Tests: lijnkoppen.test.mjs (predicate, defaults, every ribbon style
through /LE + /OPS_LineHeads, single-name /LE, legacy files),
callout-koppen.test.mjs, callout-koppen-rondgang.test.mjs (save and
reopen with the real saver and loader, no duplicates).

feat(callout): place a callout in two clicks, tip then note (#613)

A click with the callout tool used to drop a complete callout with its
note at a fixed offset from the click, so the note always had to be
moved afterwards.

Now click 1 sets the tip and creates nothing; the tool stays active
and shows the leader and the note box under the cursor; click 2 places
the note there, selects the callout and starts text editing. Esc or a
tool switch cancels a pending tip. A drag still places the callout in
one gesture (press = tip, release = note). A second click on another
page starts a new callout there; a second click on the tip itself uses
the old default offset for the note.

The state machine lives in tools/callout-plaatsing.js (pure, unit
tested); shape-tool.js feeds it and draws the preview. Status hint
drawing.calloutStep2 added to all 40 locales.

fix(tools): draw tool previews on the visible page canvas in continuous view (#616)

In continuous, book and facing view every page has its own
.annotation-canvas and the single-page overlay #annotation-canvas is not
on screen. The shared shape preview (rectangle, callout, line, cloud, ...)
and its snap indicator, the vector-snippet rubber band, the scale-region
box and the stretch crossing window were all drawn on that overlay, so
nothing showed while the gesture was in progress. Their base redraw also
went through the single-page path, so a preview drawn on a page canvas
would not have been cleared.

- New js/tools/preview-target.js: redrawForViewMode() redraws along the
  path of the current view mode, previewCtx(doelCtx) picks the canvas the
  user sees (given target, else the active page canvas in continuous view,
  else the overlay).
- drawShapePreview() takes an optional target canvas (backward compatible)
  and draws the preview and the snap indicator there; the tool context
  passes the resolved page canvas.
- Snippet, scale-region and stretch draw on ctx.canvasCtx; snippet and
  scale-region size their dashes from the effective zoom instead of a
  stale inactive viewport zoom.
- Stretch (typed displacement), array, extend and trim redraw for the
  current view mode, so their preview is cleared and their result shows
  up in continuous view.

feat(print): print modes, booklet binding/sides/creep and order buttons (#607)

- The placement group starts with a row of print modes: Normal, Multiple,
  Flyer, Booklet and Poster. Each mode shows only its own options. The mode
  follows from the stored scaling and pages-per-sheet choices, so existing
  print settings keep working; switching back remembers the last scaling and
  the last grid. Poster is no longer hidden in the scaling list and flyer and
  booklet are no longer hidden in the pages-per-sheet list.
- Page order for pages per sheet is chosen with four icon buttons that show
  the reading path (Z, reversed Z, N, reversed N).
- Booklet options: binding left or right (right-to-left books), print both
  sides, front sides only or back sides only (manual duplex on printers
  without duplex), rotate back sides 180 degrees for printers that flip on
  the long edge, and creep compensation (pages of the inner sheets move
  towards the fold, linear from 0 for the outer sheet to the chosen distance
  for the innermost sheet of every signature, clipped at the fold).
  Reverse order now reverses the sheets of a booklet instead of the reading
  order of the pages.
- The preview uses the same side list and layout as the print job
  (boekjeAfdrukZijden, boekjeIndeling): it shows rotated back sides, creep,
  a dashed fold line and the page number in every half; flyers show the page
  number in every cell. Arrows stay for pages per sheet only. None of these
  markers reach the printed output.
- A note explains that a two-sided flyer (front and back page) printed
  double-sided gives complete flyers after cutting, and a note explains
  manual duplex for booklets.
- New choices are stored with the other print settings and validated on
  restore; all new strings are translated in the 40 locales.

fix(save): keep alignment, decoration, rotation, arc, names, links and marked state over save (#619)

Properties the app offers came back empty after save and reopen. Each is
now written in the standard place where the PDF spec has one and read
back on load; a private OPS_ key is used only where the spec has none.

- Text alignment: FreeText /Q (1 centre, 2 right; left stays the default
  without /Q), read back for textboxes and callouts.
- Underline and strikethrough: text-decoration in /DS (both values) and
  as <span style="text-decoration:..."> in /RC, together with run
  colours; the appearance draws the lines per text run. The loader falls
  back to /DS when /RC has no decoration.
- Rotation of polygons and rectangular clouds: /Vertices hold the corners
  as shown on screen, the cloud appearance rotates with one cm, the angle
  goes in /OPS_Rotation; the loader turns the vertices back around the
  centre the renderer uses. On pages with /Rotate the base shape now comes
  from the displayed box, so a regular polygon no longer points another
  way in the file. Sticky notes and redaction marks keep their rotation.
- Arc: the loader reads the arc keys the saver already wrote, so an arc
  no longer reopens as a polyline.
- Marked: written as a hidden /Text reply with /StateModel /Marked and
  /State /Marked, which the loader already understood. /F has no marked
  bit (bit 2 is Hidden).
- Name, subject and links: /NM (unique per page), /Subj (the subject of
  types whose text fills /Contents, otherwise the original /Subj),
  /IRT with /RT /Group for links between annotations, /OPS_AltText and
  /OPS_IfcCategory for every type.
- Replies from the properties panel: one /Text per reply with /IRT and
  /OPS_Subtype reply, folded back under their annotation on load. Reply
  notes written by other programs stay notes and keep their link.
- Extracted annotation data is also keyed by object reference when two
  annotations share a /Rect: a review status reply took the rectangle's
  rotation, fill and private keys.

The per-page conversion moved from loader.js to
loader/annotaties-omzetten.js so the save round-trip tests run the real
loader path.

feat(flatten): flatten all markups in place, reversible on request (#615)

Flatten bakes the normal appearance of every markup into the page
content of the open document, inside a tagged marked-content block in
a content stream that carries the id of its flatten pass, and removes
the markups from /Annots. Annotations without an appearance (notes,
app-only helpers), hidden ones, form fields and links stay as they are.

With recovery allowed (default) a lossless JSON copy of the markup
model is kept in the catalog (/OPS_Flatten), per pass. A later pass
extends it; Unflatten removes only the content streams of passes it
can restore, so graphics baked by an irreversible pass stay.

- flatten-bytes.js: pure pdf-lib transform (bake matrix per PDF 12.5.5,
  /AS states, /OC layers kept as /OC BDC, popups and /IRT replies of
  baked markups removed, resources and unreachable objects cleaned up,
  page mapping when pages move after flattening)
- saver.js: bouwAnnotatieDocument() builds the document as a save would,
  annotations only, without writing; dicts carry a temporary model id
- flatten-all.js: the commands; they work on the open document via
  reloadFromBytes with one undo step, the file changes on the next save
- vector snippets referenced by a recovery copy keep their source in
  the catalog so Unflatten can restore them after reopening
- tests: byte transform, snippet sources, and a save round trip with
  the real saver and loader (flatten, save, reopen, unflatten, save,
  reopen: same markups and properties, no duplicates, no ballast)

feat(flatten): Flatten All / Unflatten All in the Comment ribbon (#615)

Two small buttons in the Edit group of the Comment tab
(#ribbon-flatten-all, #ribbon-unflatten-all). Flatten asks for
confirmation in a movable dialog with the "Allow unflattening" option
and explains that notes stay markups and that the file only changes on
save (undo reverts the step). Unflatten reports when nothing was
flattened or when the markups were flattened without recovery.
Strings in all 40 locales.

fix(blend): composite all 16 blend modes with the page and keep /BM in the file (#614)

Blend modes never reached the screen or the file, and the Format ribbon
offered only Normal and Multiply.

- New js/annotations/blend-modes.js: the 16 PDF blend modes in one table
  (model name, /BM name, canvas value). The four compound modes map to the
  hyphenated canvas names (color-dodge, color-burn, hard-light, soft-light);
  an unknown globalCompositeOperation value is silently ignored, which made
  them draw as source-over.
- Rendering: annotations sit on a transparent overlay, so a canvas blend had
  nothing to mix with. A blended annotation is now mixed with what is visible
  under it (page canvas, text-highlight layer, overlay so far) inside its
  bounding box, and only its contribution (alpha = its own coverage) is put
  on the overlay with source-over, so the visible result equals the blended
  result exactly (rendering/mengen-tegen-pagina.js). Works for the
  single-page overlay and the per-page canvases of continuous view; parts
  outside the estimated box are drawn as before. Thumbnails and offscreen
  output keep drawing natively with the mapped canvas value.
- Saver: zetDoorzichtigheidInAp writes /BM into the appearance ExtGState
  (with the alpha, also at opacity 1; as one group for arrows and textbox
  leaders). Normal writes nothing. No /OPM: overprint is unrelated to the
  non-separable modes. /BM is deliberately not also put on the annotation
  dictionary, a reader applying both would blend twice.
- Loader: /BM is read from the ExtGStates the appearance activates (name or
  array), with the PDF 2.0 annotation-level /BM as fallback, and joins the
  shared base props so every annotation type gets it back. The implicit
  multiply of text markups is not reported as a choice.
- Format ribbon: all 16 modes from the shared list, labelled in all 40
  locales, with a tooltip explaining that a blend mode is not a colour.
  Symbol insertion accepts the same list; its preview uses the mapped value.
- MCP document screenshot composites the text-highlight layer with multiply,
  as the screen does.

Tests: blend-modes, mengen-tegen-pagina (pixel math), blend-mode-ap (saver
and loader), mengmodus-rondgang (real saver and loader, second save does not
stack graphics states, back to normal removes /BM).

fix(ribbon): let ribbon popups escape the clipping groups container (#617)

.ribbon-groups-adaptive clips with overflow: hidden (it hides the groups
moved into the More flyout), so absolutely positioned popups inside it were
cut off at the bottom of the ribbon and the rest slid behind the document
tabs: the style gallery showed only its first row.

The style gallery popup, the style-tools and Align-to menus, the split-button
menu and the theme picker now use position: fixed, like the colour picker and
the overflow flyout already did. New ribbon-popup.js places a popup under its
trigger (optionally right-aligned), keeps it inside the window, flips it above
the trigger when there is no room below, and follows the trigger on scroll and
resize while open. The popups stay in their wrapper in the DOM, so the
click-outside handling is unchanged; overflow: hidden stays, so the adaptive
collapse is unaffected.

feat(screenshot): select an area and copy or save it at a chosen resolution

The Home tab's Screenshot button now starts an area selection over the
document view. After the drag a movable dialog shows a preview and offers
the resolution (screen, 96, 150, 300, 600 dpi or a custom dpi / pixel
width), the file format (PNG, or JPEG with quality) and the actions Copy to
clipboard and Save as (native save dialog). Enter runs the last used
action; Esc cancels the selection and closes the dialog. The choices are
remembered in the preferences.

The area is rendered again from the page at the chosen dpi instead of
enlarging screen pixels: page pixels through the same region renderer as
the screen (tiled), or PDF.js in the browser and for pages rotated in the
document; annotations, watermarks and text edits are drawn on top as
output, without selection frames. The view rotation is applied so the
image looks like the screen. Saved files carry the dpi in their metadata.
Images are limited to 16384 px per side and 64 megapixels.

A selection over two pages (continuous view) is clipped to the page it
overlaps most, so every pixel has one paper resolution and the gap between
the pages is not captured.

The dropdown keeps Region and Full page (both open the dialog), adds a
quick "copy area at screen resolution" without the dialog, and keeps Place
as overlay. Strings in all 40 languages.

feat(mcp): add app_capture_region to render a page area as an image

Same route as Home > Screenshot: the area (app points, or the whole page)
is rendered again at the requested dpi with the annotations, in the view
rotation the user sees, as PNG or JPEG. Returns base64, or writes the file
when an absolute path is given. Never touches the clipboard.

Registered in the Rust tool list, the dispatch, the tool metadata,
mcp-stdio/tools.json and the extension manifest; the public tool count
goes from 75 to 76.

fix(linux): link Tesseract statically so binaries need no libtesseract soname (#620)

The Linux build linked the build machine's system Tesseract through the
tesseract-rs use-system-tesseract feature, which recorded the Ubuntu 22.04
soname libtesseract.so.4 as a NEEDED entry. The raw binary, the .deb and
packages repackaged from it (such as the AUR open-pdf-studio-bin) then
failed to start on distributions that ship Tesseract 5 or no Tesseract, and
the .deb never declared the dependency.

Use build-tesseract on Linux as on Windows and macOS: Leptonica and
Tesseract are compiled from pinned sources and linked statically. The
pinned tesseract-rs already compiled its reqwest (rustls, no OpenSSL) on
Linux, so no new TLS dependency is added.

- Linux workflows no longer install libtesseract-dev/libleptonica-dev.
- ci, release and nightly cache ~/.tesseract-rs and fail when the binary
  needs libtesseract or liblept (scripts/linux-ocr-linkage-check.sh).
- The ocr_poc example loads PDFium and trained data per platform, so the
  real OCR path can be checked on Linux.

feat(packaging): add reference AUR PKGBUILD for open-pdf-studio-bin (#620)

The AUR package is maintained by the community. This reference PKGBUILD
repackages the release .deb with the runtime dependencies the binary
actually needs (WebKitGTK 4.1 stack), and no Tesseract, so the
maintainer can adopt it. Regression tests cover the static Tesseract
configuration and keep PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO in step.
ci: add temporary Linux Tesseract linkage check workflow (#620)

fix(save): keep the hatch of a box, circle, polygon or cloud over save (#621)

The hatch set in the properties panel on these four types was not
written: the shape reopened without it. The saver now writes the
OPS_Hatch keys and draws the hatch in the appearance (between fill and
border, rotated with the shape, relative to the displayed page), and the
loader reads it back. A known /PatternName from another program maps
onto the app's hatch catalogue, with /PatternColor as its colour.

Adds rondgang.testhulp.mjs (real saver plus real loader) and the first
cases of bewaren-rondgang.test.mjs.

fix(save): keep annotation keys the model does not own, and layers from other programs (#621)

A save rebuilt every annotation from the app model, so every key the
model has no place for was dropped: line styles, counts, captions,
arc angles, curved dimensions, a second callout arm, column values,
pattern names. The loader now keeps those entries as a portable copy
on the model (saver/ruwe-sleutels.js) and the saver writes them back
as new objects in the output document. Keys the app owns, OPS_ keys,
and values pointing at a page, annotation or layer are never copied
back. A measurement keeps the intent it was read with instead of
being rewritten to /PolygonDimension.

An optional content group without /OPS_LayerId that an annotation
points at is now read as a layer (name, visibility, lock, print
state). On save the same group is reused and stamped with the layer
id, instead of all markups collapsing onto the default layer. Groups
no annotation points at stay out of the annotation layer panel.

fix(packaging): declare every runtime library owner in the AUR PKGBUILD (#620)

namcap on Arch maps the binary's NEEDED entries to dbus, xz, lcms2, libgcc and libstdc++ in addition to the WebKitGTK stack; gcc-libs is split into libgcc and libstdc++ on current Arch. Linux bundles no PDFium worker sidecar, so the comment no longer mentions one.
ci: let pacman resolve PKGBUILD dependencies in the #620 check

fix(save): keep counts and extension annotations over save (#621)

- The app's own count marker had no saver branch and disappeared on
  save. It is now written as a /Circle with an appearance that draws the
  numbered dot, its number, category and marker style in OPS_ keys, and
  read back as a count.

fix(print): keep page content upright in pages-per-sheet unless Auto-rotate fits it better (#623)

With pages per sheet (and flyers) the chosen sheet orientation was also
used to build each page's own print page. A landscape page with a
confirmed portrait orientation therefore landed rotated on a portrait
print page before being shrunk into its cell, so the content stayed
sideways. Auto-rotate had no say in it at all, so unticking it changed
nothing.

Sheet orientation and page-in-cell rotation are now separate rules:
- the sheet: a Page Setup orientation confirmed for the document is
  fixed; otherwise the best-fitting orientation is chosen;
- the page: its print page always keeps the page's own orientation;
  with Auto-rotate on it turns a quarter (counter-clockwise) inside its
  cell only when it comes out larger, never on a tie; with Auto-rotate
  off it is never rotated;
- a booklet always keeps its pages upright.

The preview and the print job share the same rules: bronKeuzes moves
to print-meerperblad.js, kiesBlad/velIndeling take the rotation flag,
maakMeerPerBlad draws turned pages with a rotation, and the dialog
draws them through beeldInCel.

fix(scale-region): fill and border follow the annotation's own properties (#611)

The scale region fill was drawn at a hard-coded 0.10 * (opacity || 1), so
the Opacity control barely changed it and an opacity of 0 was drawn as
100 %. The file had no appearance stream and the loader ignored /CA, so
the opacity was also lost after save and reopen.

- One style rule (scale-region-style.js) for screen, file and panel:
  border and badge use color/opacity; the fill uses fillColor (falls back
  to color) and fillOpacity. Without an own fillOpacity the fill stays at
  10 % of opacity, so existing documents look exactly as before.
- Properties panel: Fill Color (without a None option) and a new Fill
  Opacity row for scale regions, single and multi selection; the panel
  shows the effective values. New string in all 40 locales.
- Saver writes an appearance stream (fill /ca and dashed border /CA in
  their own graphics states), /IC for an own fill colour and
  OPS_FillOpacity whenever fillOpacity is set.
- Loader reads /CA, /IC and OPS_FillOpacity for scale regions; the alpha
  derived from the appearance does not become an own value.
- XFDF export/import carries opacity, interior-color and opsfillopacity.
- Flatten all keeps scale regions as markups (measuring aid), as before.

fix(stamps): bake stamp and image rotation into the appearance, drop /OPS_Rotation

Stamps and images took their rotation from the private /OPS_Rotation key
while the appearance stream (what every other reader draws) said something
else. Old screenshots pasted on /Rotate 90 pages (e.g. -CP-21
Constructieoverzicht) carry /OPS_Rotation -90 and an unrotated appearance
with screen-oriented pixels: the app turned them counter-clockwise and
squeezed them, other readers squeezed them too.

Saver (stamp, text stamp, image, signature):
- no /OPS_Rotation any more; the in-app rotation and the page /Rotate
  compensation go into one rotation cm around the BBox centre
  (saver/stempel-draaiing.js), Matrix stays identity, /Rect is the
  bounding box of the rotated box. Without rotation the output is
  byte-identical to the previous page compensation.
- text stamps get a clip on their box so the loader can read the box back.

Loader:
- /OPS_Rotation is ignored for /Stamp; box and rotation are derived from
  /Rect, /BBox, /Matrix and the content cm's (loader/stempel-geometrie.js,
  read by loader/stempel-ap.js). Bitmaps whose box is derived this way are
  'visual'; composite appearances, mirrored or skewed ones fall back to the
  previous /Rect-based behaviour.
- legacy screenshots on /Rotate 90/270 pages (unrotated appearance, pixel
  aspect clearly matching the page-rotated rect and not the unrotated one)
  are shown upright, filling their on-screen rect; near-square bitmaps are
  never treated this way.
- rendered fallback crops are never rotated again.
- /SquareImage annotations use the same appearance-derived box.

real saver and loader on /Rotate 0/90/180/270 pages, with and without
rotation, saved twice, plus fixture-free legacy and SquareImage cases.

fix(stamps): keep the existing on-screen look of stamps from older files

The previous commit derived every stamp's box and rotation from its
appearance. That changed how existing files look in the app: stamps whose
rotation lived only in /OPS_Rotation (-CP-21-3/-4) lost it, and bitmaps
drawn unrotated on a /Rotate 90 page (VO Constructie) turned with the page
instead of reading upright as before.

The loader now trusts the appearance only when this saver wrote it, and
shows every other file exactly as before:
- the saver puts a clip on exactly the image box right after the rotation
  cm; an appearance with that clip and without /OPS_Rotation is our own and
  is shown as drawn (kiesStempelWeergave, eigenAp).

- the legacy screenshot rule (CP-21) still wins: upright, filling the
  on-screen rect, ignoring its /OPS_Rotation.
- raw PDF-space pixels without rotation are written back without the clip,

Saving bakes the shown rotation into the appearance, so other readers then

commit.message:
fix(stamps): show stamps as their appearance draws them, never save a distortion

Stamps whose appearance places the bitmap unambiguously were still shown
in their /Rect as it appears on screen, with the old /OPS_Rotation or
/Matrix angle. When the appearance draws the bitmap in a differently
shaped or rotated box, that view squeezes it, and since saving bakes the
shown view into the appearance, other readers then showed the distortion
too. Example: VO Constructie, a landscape floor plan drawn unrotated on a
/Rotate 90 page (so turned with the page, portrait /Rect on screen) was
shown upright and squeezed, and a save wrote it that way.

kiesStempelWeergave now shows a stamp exactly as its appearance draws it
(box, centre, rotation, pixels upright in that box), as every other reader
does, with two legacy exceptions written by older versions of the app:
- a non-zero /OPS_Rotation (the appearance did not rotate the bitmap
  itself, e.g. -CP-21-3/-4): the /Rect on screen in that rotation;
- old screenshots on /Rotate 90/270 pages (CP-21): upright, filling the
  on-screen /Rect.
When the drawn box coincides with the on-screen /Rect in the same
rotation (within 0.5 pt or 0.5 %), the /Rect is kept, so files that
already looked right do not move by rounding noise.

Also affected: the /Matrix-rotated symbols of -CP-21-2 and tekening-2
are now shown at the size and aspect their appearance draws (as other
readers show them) instead of filling the bounding /Rect.

Tests: the VO-like and -CP-21-2 round trips now expect the drawn geometry
and check that two saves leave the external geometry unchanged; new
cases for a rotation cm in the appearance and for the /Rect tolerance;
a guard test checks for every legacy and current case that the saved
appearance draws the aspect and rotation the app showed.

Add headless mode for test instances (OPDS_HEADLESS=1)

Release gates, sweeps and measurements start their own test instance of
the app. Its window popped up on the desktop and took focus. With
OPDS_HEADLESS=1 next to --mcp-server or OPDS_DETACHED=1 the instance
never appears on screen and never takes focus; a normal start ignores
the variable and behaves exactly as before.

- The configured window is created hidden, unfocused, non-activatable
  and without taskbar button, with a fixed inner size (1200x800 or
  OPDS_HEADLESS_SIZE=WxH). A plugin then parks every window outside all
  monitors (nearest to the primary monitor, so the DPI stays the same),
  shows it without activating it and parks it again if Windows moves it
  back on screen.
- WebView2 gets CalculateNativeWinOcclusion disabled and the
  background-throttling switches, merged with an existing
  WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS (debug port kept, one
  --disable-features list, idempotent for torn-off tab instances).
- The dialog plugin is replaced by a stub with the same name and
  commands: file pickers answer null, message boxes the dismiss answer,
  each with a log line. alert/confirm/prompt/print are suppressed too.
- Every focus/show/unminimize path (single instance, PrtScn, file-open
  activation, print queue window, maximize/fullscreen/minimize) is
  skipped, and commands that bring another program to the front
  (browser, Explorer, mail client, settings, printer properties,
  sign-in) refuse with a log line.
- Torn-off tab instances inherit the environment and start headless;
  the print queue window is created hidden and parked as well.
- Test start scripts set OPDS_HEADLESS=1.

Tests: pure rules (activation, size, argument merging, parking
position, dialog answers) in headless/regels.rs, runnable standalone
with rustc --test; JS guards and source checks in
js/core/headless.test.mjs.

Document OPDS_HEADLESS for test instances

Release test protocol and the extension rig description now start test instances headless and explain what the variable does.

commit.message: fix(android): build the headless taskbar call only on desktop
chore: version to 2026.43.2

fix(save): drop replaced annotation objects so files stop growing per save

pdf-lib writes every object in its context, reachable or not. Each save
replaces all managed annotations with fresh ones from the model, so the old
annotation dicts, appearance streams, fonts and images stayed in the file,
and the new objects were always numbered above the old maximum. The xref
table grew by the whole annotation set on every save (VO Constructie.pdf:
240 -> 488 -> 731 entries over two saves).

Before serializing, the saver now:
- updates form field appearances and flushes pdf-lib's pending embeds, so
  nothing is created after the cleanup;
- removes every object that is unreachable from the trailer;
- moves the objects created by this save into the lowest free object
  numbers. Existing objects keep their numbers (foreign OCG layer ids depend
  on them), and numbers still targeted by a dangling reference are never
  reused. Encrypted documents are cleaned but not renumbered.

Saving is a full rewrite as before; signed documents keep going through the
existing signature confirmation, and signature dictionaries stay reachable
through the AcroForm.

VO Constructie.pdf now stays at 278 xref entries over repeated saves, with
identical renders.

Add crash log, panic hook and recovery store for unsaved work

Rust side of crash recovery:

- crashlog.rs: crash log in <data dir>/OpenPDFStudio/logs/crash-<date>.log
  (UTC day files, 1 MiB cap per day, 10 days kept, no document content).
  A panic hook writes message, location, thread and backtrace, then asks
  the frontend for an emergency snapshot (event herstel-nood) and waits up
  to 3 s; not on the main thread, where the WebView cannot answer, and at
  most once per 60 s. WebView2 ProcessFailed is hooked through COM (Windows,
  desktop only) and logged.
- herstel.rs: recovery folder <data dir>/OpenPDFStudio/herstel with a
  per-process running marker (pid + process start time) that is only
  removed after a clean frontend shutdown; commands to write snapshot files
  atomically, list, read, rename, delete, claim an offer, check process
  liveness, copy a snapshot to a working file or a chosen path, and a test
  panic command that only works with OPDS_CRASH_TEST=1.
- Paths are restricted to the recovery folder; the user's original file is
  never written by this code.

Snapshot unsaved documents and offer recovery after a crash

- js/herstel: watches open documents every 5 s. A document with unsaved
  changes gets a recovery snapshot about 30 s after the last change, and at
  most every 2 minutes while changes continue (longer after a slow
  snapshot). The snapshot is the full PDF the normal saver would write
  (new bouwMomentopname mode: no write, no "saved" state, no messages,
  more frequent yields), stored with a manifest (original path and its
  size/mtime at open, title, time, pages, app version) under
  OpenPDFStudio/herstel/<instance>_<session>_<doc>. Only the latest
  snapshot per document is kept; PDF first, manifest last.
- Snapshots are removed after a successful save, on closing a tab (also
  with "don't save") and on a clean exit. Password-protected documents are
  never snapshotted; PDFs above 64 MiB are skipped and logged once.
- window error and unhandledrejection write the crash log and trigger an
  immediate snapshot of all modified documents, guarded against recursion
  and throttled.
- On start the primary instance logs unclean exits of dead instances,
  removes snapshots older than 14 days, and offers what dead instances (or
  a crashed WebView of this process) left behind in the Windows-style
  dialog "Niet-opgeslagen werk herstellen": Open (new unsaved document whose
  save target is the original, marked as recovered in its tab), Save as,
  Delete, Delete all and Later. Headless instances log the offer instead.
  Snapshots of other running instances are never touched.
- Texts in all 40 locales; unit tests for scheduling, manifest, atomic
  snapshot writes, cleanup and marker rules with several instances, the
  error handler, and the snapshot mode of the saver.

Reload the main window after a WebView renderer crash

- When WebView2 reports that the render process of the main window exited
  or became unresponsive, reload that window automatically (desktop only).
  The new frontend session then offers the snapshots of the previous
  session through the existing recovery path.
- Crash-loop limit: at most 2 automatic reloads per 5 minutes. After that
  the window is left as it is and the limit is logged; on the next
  successful load the app shows an in-app message (headless: log only).
- Right before a reload nothing can be flushed any more: the renderer that
  held the document model is gone, so the latest regular or emergency
  snapshot is what comes back. Documented in crashlog.rs and herstel.js.
- A successful frontend start after a reload clears the "WebView failed"
  state, so a later clean exit still removes the running marker.
- Unit tests for the reload decision and loop limit (Rust) and for the
  message/log decision after a reload (JS); new text in all locales.

commit.message:
Carry annotations, form fields, bookmarks and more along when merging PDFs

Merging only kept the bare pages. pdf-lib's copyPages did copy each page's
/Annots into the bytes, but:

- the app marked every page of the reloaded document as loaded, so the
  annotations of the merged pages never reached the annotation model: they
  were not drawn (pages render without annotations) and the next save, which
  replaces the annotations of a loaded page with those of the model, dropped
  them;
- references to a page (/P of an annotation, link and outline destinations)
  became loose copies of that page outside the page tree, so internal links
  went nowhere;
- form fields, bookmarks, named destinations, layers (/OCProperties) and page
  labels of the catalog were left behind;
- a source file that was open in the app was read from disk, without its
  unsaved annotations.

samenvoegen.js now merges per source file with one object copier in which
every source page is first given its new reference, so all references to a
page land on the page in the result. Per source it merges the AcroForm
(clashing field names get the file name as suffix, /DR completed, inherited
/DA and /Q kept, /NeedAppearances kept), places the bookmarks under one
bookmark named after the file, merges named destinations (renaming clashes
and the references to them), layers (visibility, order grouped per file,
locks, radio groups; a layer of this app with the same id stays one layer),
page labels and embedded files. Signature values are removed: a merged
document is not signed. Rotation, crop box and user unit come along with
the page.

In the app, reloadFromBytes now loads the annotations of pages that are new
after a page operation (and of pages that were not loaded yet) before
drawing and before the undo state is recorded, adds annotation layers it
finds, and returns the annotations in the model for redo. Merging adds the
page labels of the inserted pages, merges the bookmark model (own bookmarks
move with their page; undo and redo restore them), keeps unsaved form values
of the document, and takes an open source file as the app has it, through
the saver's snapshot, without writing anything. The MCP merge answer lists
per file what came along.

Warn in the merge dialog when a file is digitally signed

Merging removes the signatures of signed files, so the merged document is
not signed. The dialog checks each added file and shows one warning line,
in all locales.

Keep the empty label of pages before the first label range when merging

A document whose /PageLabels start after its first page shows no label for
the pages before. Merging gave them a page number instead; they now get an
empty range, in the document and in each merged file.

- Tests for formatting, parsing, legacy lookup, IFC export, search and a
  save/reopen round trip of an old document.

docs(assistant): use K100/5 for square hollow sections in prompts and MCP help

The structural layout tool description (Rust and mcp-stdio/tools.json),
the assistant system prompt and the construction overview skill now give
K100/5 as the example for a square hollow section and "Koker 100x50x5"
for a rectangular one.

feat(input): one number parser that accepts comma and dot

Add core/getal-invoer.js, a single parser for every number the user types:
- comma and dot are both the decimal separator ("0,1" = "0.1");
- surrounding spaces and a leading sign are allowed;
- thousand separators only where unambiguous ("1.234,5", "1,234.5",
  "1.234.567"); a single separator is always the decimal;
- scale notations: "1:100" (leesVerhouding), "0,5x" / "2x" / "50%"
  (leesFactor) and "2,5 m" (leesGetalMetEenheid);
- invalid input gives NaN (leesGetal) or null (leesGetalOfNull), as
  callers expect; leesGetalBegin/leesGeheelGetal are drop-in
  replacements for parseFloat/parseInt;
- toonGetal shows a value with the decimal separator of a language.

The scattered comma-to-dot helpers now use it: shape and paper sizes,
bar series, poster print, screen calibration, page shift, document
split, CAD pen widths, drawing scales, the symbol placement scale and
the properties store. The status-bar zoom field reads "62,5" and
"62.5" through leesZoomInvoer.

feat(input): every number field accepts both decimal separators

An <input type="number"> in the WebView rejects one of the two decimal
separators depending on the locale, and the field then silently becomes
empty. All number fields in js/ are now text fields marked data-getal
with inputmode="decimal"; ui/getal-veld.js gives them number-field
behaviour back:
- `value` returns the canonical number text ("0.1") or '' for invalid
  input, so existing parseFloat/Number/parseInt handlers keep working
  whichever separator was typed;
- assigned values are shown with the decimal separator of the app
  language ("0,1" in Dutch, "0.1" in English) and re-shown after a
  language change; non-numbers become empty, as in a number field;
- while the user types, a fallback or clamp written back by a handler
  ("0" -> 1) waits until Enter, Escape or leaving the field, so "0,1"
  can be typed at all;
- ArrowUp/ArrowDown step by step within min/max; letters are refused.

Text fields that read numbers themselves now use the shared parser too:
the properties-panel combo boxes (line width, opacity, font size; they
stripped the comma, so "0,5" became 5), the status-bar zoom field
("62,5" and "62.5"), the measurement scale dialog ("2,5 m"), the scale
region ratio, the custom ratio of the calibration dialog (decimals now
allowed), the box size overlay (shown in the app language), the
measured length, poster overlap, style type and drawing settings.

Stylesheets select number fields by [data-getal]. A source check keeps
type="number" and loose comma-to-dot parsers out of js/.

commit.message:
fix(stamps): rounded text stamps on screen, own stamp name, redraw after image decode

- A text stamp is drawn with rounded corners on screen, like the appearance the
  saver writes (it was a sharp rectangle).
- A text stamp with its own appearance is saved under its own /Name instead of a
  standard one ('Draft'): some editors draw their built-in stamp instead as soon
  as the stamp is edited or rotated. The real name stays in /Subj and
  OPS_StampName.
- A stamp image that is still decoding when first drawn is redrawn when it is
  ready; before, it stayed invisible until the next redraw (for example a scroll).

fix(touch): finger strokes draw in the signature pad and no longer break off on the page (#671)

The signature pad listened to mouse events only; a finger drag sends pointer
and touch events, so no stroke was recorded. It now uses pointer events with
pointer capture and touch-action: none.

On the page, the browser took a finger drag as a scroll gesture after a few
millimetres and sent pointercancel, so freehand strokes broke off. While a
drawing or placing tool is active the drawing surface now has
touch-action: none (select and hand still scroll with a finger), and a
cancelled pointer finishes the gesture at its last move.
Merge branch 'fix/671-touch-drawing' into integratie/issues-2026.43
Merge pull request #670 into integratie/issues-2026.43

fix(stamps): redraw the continuous view too once a stamp image has decoded

The load handler from #670 called redrawAnnotations(), which only paints the
single-page canvas. In the continuous view the stamp stayed invisible until
the next redraw. Use one helper that picks the active view, as the tile and
system-symbol callbacks already did.

build(version): one YYYY.W.N version for every package, crate and bundle (#667)

Every version field in the repository now carries the app number
2026.43.4: the internal crates (open-pdf-render, pdfium-worker,
open-pdf-cad, open-pdf-cmyk, open-pdf-thumbnails) with their Cargo.lock
entries, the mcp-stdio bridge and the snapcraft.yaml placeholder.

bump-version.js derives the workspace crates from the root Cargo.toml,
sets every field, rejects a version outside YYYY.W.N (year, ISO week
1-53 without a leading zero, sequence number from 0) and gains a --check
mode that compares all fields with a release tag without writing.

release.yml runs that check in create-release, before a draft release or
any build exists, so a pushed tag or workflow_dispatch input that does
not match the version fields stops the run.

versievelden.test.mjs (unit list) checks that all fields are equal and
follow the schema, that every tracked package.json and Cargo.toml with a
version is covered by bump-version.js, that a bump only touches version
fields, and that no MSI target or WiX config comes back: WiX caps the
major version at 255, so YYYY.W.N cannot be an MSI version. It replaces
the narrower consistency test in release-config.test.mjs.

flake.nix and the AUR PKGBUILD package an already published release with
its hash; they stay one release behind and are only checked against the
schema.
Merge branch 'fix/667-version-scheme' into integratie/issues-2026.43

fix(annotations): ribbon colour and width style the active tool (#668)

The Colour and Width fields under Properties on the Annotation tab only
wrote two ribbon signals. Every tool read its own style preference first
and used those signals only as a fallback, so new annotations never got
them. Freehand did the opposite: the ribbon value overrode its own style
preference, which the properties panel sets for the active tool.

Colour and Width now act on the same target as the Format toolbar: the
selection, otherwise the next annotation of the active drawing tool (its
style preferences, so the choice is kept for the next object of that
tool), or the symbol insert session. Without a target they are disabled
and explain what they apply to. Freehand reads its own preference first,
like every other tool.

While a drawing tool with a style is active and nothing is selected, the
contextual Format tab now appears (the ribbon does not switch to it) and
sets the style of the next annotation. Options the tool does not draw
with stay disabled. The tool defaults in the properties panel follow a
change made there.

The style mapping per annotation type moves to core/stijl-mapping.js so
the new tool format module stays free of app imports.

fix(text-layer): even selection highlight without overlapping runs (#506)

After the last tab was closed, the viewport fitted a hidden 0x0 container
(zoom = 1 / page height). The next document built its PDF.js text layer at
that scale, so every run was measured at about 0.02 px, where Chromium
returns roughly half the width: --scale-x became about 2 and each span was
twice too wide. The single page view does not rebuild the layer on zoom, so
the selection boxes overlapped (darker bands at word boundaries) and ran
past the text.

- Measure the text layer at scale 1 or more. The scale only sets the
  measuring size, so the layer geometry is otherwise unchanged.
- Paint the selection as one group: an opaque pastel without a glyph
  colour, with the text layer multiplied onto the page. Overlaps keep one
  tint and the real glyphs stay visible instead of being redrawn in a
  fallback font.
- Drop the duplicate selection rule that pdf-viewport.js injected.

fix(text-edit): keep table borders and sharp text when editing PDF text (#669)

Editing existing PDF text hid the vector lines around it and made the
replacement look blurred.

- The live view covered the old text with one white rectangle over the
  whole block. A table row is one block and the width came from a
  character-count estimate plus half an em, so the cell borders of the
  edited row disappeared. The cover is now one tight area per original
  text run, filled with a rendering of the page without text (PDF.js with
  the text and image operations filtered out), so lines that touch or
  cross the old text stay visible.
- In the single-page viewport the replacement text was painted on the
  annotation overlay, which is sized in CSS pixels and stretched on
  screens with a devicePixelRatio above 1. The viewport now paints text
  edits on the page canvas with its device-pixel transform.
- PDF.js reports unresolved or non-embedded fonts as 'sans-serif', which
  matched the serif check, so the replacement came back in Times-Roman
  on screen and in the saved file.
- When the saver cannot cut the original run in place, it now covers
  each original run tightly instead of the whole block.
