chore: version to 2026.43.6

fix(mcp): never return the contents of password fields from app_read_ui

app_read_ui returned the value of every input, so a password typed in the
open-password dialog, the protect dialog or the assistant key field was
readable by any MCP client. A filled password field now reports a fixed
mask, an empty one stays empty, so the length does not leak either.

feat(export): protect a copy of the document with a password (AES-256)

File > Export > Protect with Password saves a protected copy of the open
document, using the PDF standard security handler (ISO 32000-2, V 5 / R 6,
AES-256), so other PDF viewers open it with the password.

- Open password: without it the document does not open (empty = anyone can).
- Rights password and permissions: print, high-quality print, copy, change,
  annotate, fill forms, insert/delete/rotate pages.
- Passwords are normalised with SASLprep as the standard requires; an empty
  rights password becomes a random 256-bit value nobody knows; password and key
  bytes are zeroised after use; a minimum of 6 characters is enforced.
- The open document is never changed; the copy is written next to it under a
  new name, after saving unsaved changes when the user agrees.
- Encryption is done in Rust (new module pdf_beveiliging.rs) on top of lopdf,
  which reads the file and writes the result; strings and streams are encrypted
  and the /Encrypt dictionary is added.

fix(protect): copy from the saved file and refuse password-opened documents

- After a page edit the document renders from a temporary working copy
  (filePath) while the saved file is saveTargetPath. The protected copy was
  made from the working copy and missed everything saved after the edit,
  such as new annotations. Use saveTargetPath || filePath, as e-mail and
  signing already do.
- A document opened with a password is read-only and is never saved, not
  even as a copy. Its filePath is the decrypted working copy, so a protected
  copy with only a rights password opened without any password. Refuse it
  in the export panel (before passwords are typed) and in the module.

fix(protect): drop stale xref links and detect a direct /Encrypt entry

- lopdf rewrites the whole file as one section but keeps /Prev and
  /XRefStm from the source trailer. For an incrementally updated or
  linearized source the protected copy pointed at a cross-reference
  section that no longer exists; strict readers reported a damaged file
  and rebuilt the table. Remove both keys before writing.
- lopdf's is_encrypted() only sees an /Encrypt reference. A source with
  the encryption dictionary directly in the trailer was encrypted a second
  time and its pages came out empty. Refuse any /Encrypt entry.

fix(protect): keep every object, leave signature contents clear, prepare passwords like pdf.js

- lopdf (0.34 and newer) decodes the PNG "Average" predictor wrongly
  (a + b / 2 instead of (a + b) / 2). In a cross-reference stream with such
  a row the entry points to the wrong place and the object silently goes
  missing; a sample drawing lost two annotation appearances this way. After
  loading, objects listed in the cross-reference table but not loaded are
  looked up by their "N G obj" header and the file is read again with an
  extra cross-reference section that points to them. If anything is still
  missing the command refuses with INCOMPLETE instead of writing a lossy copy.
- The /Contents of /Sig and /DocTimeStamp dictionaries is no longer
  encrypted (ISO 32000-2, 7.6.2).
- Passwords get the SASLprep mapping step and NFKC only, as pdf.js does; the
  prohibition rules are dropped, so passwords with an emoji or with Hebrew or
  Arabic followed by digits are accepted again. When opening a protected file
  the app now also tries the prepared and the 127-byte forms of what was
  typed, since PDFium prepares nothing itself.
- Errors are fixed codes (NEED_PASSWORD, ALREADY_ENCRYPTED, READ_FAILED,
  INCOMPLETE, WRITE_FAILED) with an optional detail, translated by the
  front end.
- The target is written through atomic_file. The hash buffers, the prepared
  passwords, the UE/OE keys and the file key are zeroised, also on error.

fix(protect): portable passwords, signed-document warning, translated errors, compact dialog

- The dialog refuses passwords longer than 127 UTF-8 bytes and passwords
  that the PDF password preparation would change (full-width letters,
  special spaces, invisible or control characters), so the password works
  exactly as typed in every reader, including the app itself.
- A signed document asks the same question as "Save As" to another file:
  the copy is rewritten, so its signatures are no longer valid.
- Error codes from the Rust command are mapped to translated messages.
- The card is disabled in the browser build, like PDF/X and CAD.
- The dialog uses the existing compact field and checkbox styles, wide
  password fields, small hints and the rights in two columns.
- Comments in Dutch, like the rest of js/.

i18n(protect): translate the password protection texts into all locales

All 32 dialog texts and the two export panel texts are now translated in
every locale instead of falling back to English, and the texts name no
specific PDF programs.
